meta.docSubtitle: 12 confirmed flows · HD Portal + Salesforce + ComputerEase + DocHub + GCP + Deltek · Most answers are pre-filled — please verify and correct
meta.source: Scoping calls with Peerless Fence team — contact: Ashley (operations lead)

bizContext.snapshot:
Right now, your team is manually moving data between six systems every single day. Ashley enters leads from HD Portal into Salesforce, then manually creates customer records in ComputerEase, then uploads contracts, then enters deposit amounts, then attaches work orders back to Salesforce. Each step is a chance for data to get lost or entered wrong. You said it yourself: 'I don't like your view. It looks terrible... I have to click on a couple of different things just to get around.' That friction is costing you time and accuracy.

On go-live Monday, those manual steps stop. Leads sync automatically every 10 minutes. Contracts flow to DocHub for digital signatures without Ashley printing and scanning. Job data moves from Salesforce to ComputerEase without re-entry. The systems talk to each other instead of you talking to all of them.

Most answers in this form are already filled in from your scoping calls. Please verify them and correct anything that's changed.

journeyCards.label: Phase 1 — Connected
journeyCards.headline: HD Portal, Salesforce, ComputerEase, and DocHub become a single data path
journeyCards.body:
Things that stop on go-live Monday:
  • UC1: Ashley manually checking HD Portal for new leads and copying them into Salesforce — now syncs every 10 minutes automatically
  • UC3: Ashley manually creating customer records in ComputerEase from HD Portal lead data — now triggered by lead sync
  • UC5: Ashley manually verifying quotes from HD Portal and entering them into Salesforce — now flows directly
  • UC4: Ashley printing contracts, getting signatures, scanning them back — now DocHub captures digital signatures for contract types 299A, 299B, 118
  • UC6: Ashley manually attaching ComputerEase work orders to Salesforce sales orders — now linked via API
  • UC7: Ashley manually uploading signed contracts from HD Portal into ComputerEase — now automated document flow
  • UC12: Ashley manually entering deposit amounts and payment terms from HD Portal into ComputerEase — now synced with contract data

journeyCards.label: Phase 2 — Automated
journeyCards.headline: Deposit verification and quote validation trigger job entry without human dispatch
journeyCards.body:
Potential flows under evaluation:

  • PF1 — Automated Deposit Verification: When a deposit hits HD Portal, ComputerEase automatically verifies it and triggers job entry — no more manual backend reporting checks
  • PF2 — Quote Line Item Validation: Quote line items (material type, picket type, post caps, gates) automatically validate against contract specs before job entry — flags mismatches for Ashley to review
  • PF3 — Intelligent Document Processing: Contract documents automatically extract key data (permit date, deposit amount, signature legibility) and validate against business rules — exceptions flagged for manual review only

journeyCards.label: Phase 3 — Agentic
journeyCards.headline: AI reads the Salesforce data foundation Phase 1 built
journeyCards.body: Once Salesforce becomes the single source of truth for leads, opportunities, and contracts, Salesforce AgentForce can read that data model to answer questions, flag risks, and suggest next steps — all without Ashley clicking through multiple systems.

p0Blockers.title: Enable ComputerEase API Access
p0Blockers.clientAction: — Contact Deltek support and submit a vendor support ticket to enable API access for ComputerEase. Request configuration of the CE Live Service relay and confirm that your API version is v26 or higher. Verify that sandbox and production environments match so we can test safely before going live.

p0Blockers.title: Harden GCP Firewall Rules for ComputerEase VM
p0Blockers.clientAction: — Work with your IT team or GCP administrator to lock down the firewall rules on the ComputerEase VM. Right now SSH and RDP access is open from anywhere — that's a security risk. Restrict access to only the IP addresses that need it, and isolate the ComputerEase network so only authorized systems can reach it.

p0Blockers.title: Verify Salesforce API User Permissions and Admin Access
p0Blockers.clientAction: — Confirm that the Salesforce user account we'll use for the integration has the right permissions to read and write data. Make sure a Salesforce admin has full access to configure API integrations. We'll set up a read-only API user for ComputerEase data sync so nothing gets accidentally changed.

p0Blockers.title: Obtain Home Depot Service Center Portal API Credentials
p0Blockers.clientAction: — Contact Marius on the Home Depot Portal team and request API credentials for the lead generation API. Discuss whether they support webhooks for real-time lead updates or if we need to poll every 10 minutes. This is the starting point for all lead data flowing into Salesforce.

p0Blockers.title: Configure DocHub for Digital Signature Capture and API Access
p0Blockers.clientAction: — Set up DocHub to capture digital signatures on your three contract types: 299A, 299B, and 118. Establish a document storage and retrieval API so signed contracts automatically flow back into Salesforce and ComputerEase without Ashley handling paper.

sections.title: Use Cases & Integration Flows
sections.bodyHtml:
UC7

Contract Document Upload to ComputerEase (event-triggered)

▼

HD Portal (Home Depot Service Center) → ComputerEase · Contract · Event: signed contract available in HD Portal

1

Which specific contract document types (299A, 299B, 118) are required to be present before a job record can be created in ComputerEase — and is there a defined order or dependency between them?

2

Where are the signed contract documents stored in HD Portal — are they accessible via a document download API endpoint, or only through the portal UI?

3

Does ComputerEase support document attachment via API (e.g., attaching a PDF to a job record programmatically), or does document upload require manual UI interaction only?

→ See Section 3.7 for the pre-filled UC7 field mapping table.

In ScopeDataSkate will build an automated flow that detects newly signed contracts in HD Portal, retrieves the associated document files (299A, 299B, 118), and attaches them to the corresponding ComputerEase job record via API.
Assumes Pre-existsHD Portal API credentials are obtained from the HD Portal team (Marius) prior to build. ComputerEase API access is enabled by Deltek support with CE Live Service relay configured and API version v26+ confirmed. A matching ComputerEase job record already exists at the time of document upload.
Out of ScopeDataSkate will not create the ComputerEase job record as part of this flow. DataSkate will not validate document content or perform OCR/IDP on contract documents in this flow. DataSkate will not manage document versioning or archival within ComputerEase.
UC8

Task Creation for Material and Labor (event-triggered)

▼

Salesforce → ComputerEase · Task · Event: job record created or project milestone reached in Salesforce

1

What specific task types are created in Salesforce for material purchases and labor assignments — and what data fields (e.g., assignee, due date, cost code, quantity) are required on each task before it can be pushed to ComputerEase?

2

Is there a one-to-one relationship between a Salesforce project task and a ComputerEase cost code entry, or can a single task map to multiple cost codes?

3

Who currently creates tasks in Salesforce — is it Ashley exclusively, or do other team members (e.g., project managers, field supervisors) also create tasks that need to flow to ComputerEase?

→ See Section 3.8 for the pre-filled UC8 field mapping table.

In ScopeDataSkate will build an automated flow that listens for task creation events in Salesforce and creates corresponding cost code or labor entries in ComputerEase via API, mapping task fields to ComputerEase job record fields.
Assumes Pre-existsSalesforce API user permissions are verified and admin access is confirmed for API integration configuration. ComputerEase API access is enabled by Deltek support with CE Live Service relay configured. Cost codes and labor categories are pre-configured in ComputerEase before the flow runs.
Out of ScopeDataSkate will not create or manage cost codes or labor categories within ComputerEase. DataSkate will not sync task status updates back from ComputerEase to Salesforce in this flow. DataSkate will not enforce business rules for task assignment or approval workflows within Salesforce.
UC9

Appointment Scheduling Sync (event-triggered)

▼

HD Portal (Home Depot Service Center) → Salesforce · Appointment · Event: sales rep schedules consultation appointment in HD Portal

1

When an appointment is scheduled in HD Portal, what data fields are included (e.g., customer name, address, appointment date/time, assigned sales rep, job type) — and which of these need to appear on the Salesforce calendar event?

2

Does HD Portal provide a webhook or push notification when an appointment is created or modified, or does the sync rely on polling the HD Portal API at a defined interval?

3

Should appointment updates or cancellations made in HD Portal also sync back to Salesforce, or is this a one-time create-only flow?

→ See Section 3.9 for the pre-filled UC9 field mapping table.

In ScopeDataSkate will build a flow that detects new appointment records in HD Portal (via polling or webhook) and creates a corresponding calendar event or activity record in Salesforce, mapping all relevant appointment fields.
Assumes Pre-existsHD Portal API credentials are obtained from the HD Portal team (Marius) prior to build. Salesforce API user permissions are verified and admin access is confirmed. Salesforce calendar or activity object is configured and accessible via API.
Out of ScopeDataSkate will not sync appointment data back from Salesforce to HD Portal. DataSkate will not manage sales rep assignment logic or territory routing within Salesforce. DataSkate will not send customer-facing appointment confirmation notifications.
UC10

GCP Infrastructure Configuration (event-triggered)

▼

Google Cloud Platform (GCP) → ComputerEase · Infrastructure · Event: integration project initiation / environment provisioning

1

⚠️ CRITICAL: GCP firewall rules currently allow SSH and RDP access from any source IP. Has your IT team or GCP administrator been engaged to restrict SSH/RDP access to authorized IP ranges only and configure network isolation for the ComputerEase VM?

2

What is the current network path from the MuleSoft integration layer to the ComputerEase VM on GCP — is there an existing API gateway, VPN, or private service connect configuration in place, or will this need to be established?

3

Who owns the GCP project and has administrative access to modify firewall rules and networking configuration — is this managed internally or through a third-party IT provider?

→ See Section 3.10 for the pre-filled UC10 field mapping table.

In ScopeDataSkate will document the required GCP firewall rule changes and network configuration needed to enable secure API access from the MuleSoft integration layer to the ComputerEase VM, and will validate connectivity as part of environment setup.
Assumes Pre-existsGCP firewall rules are hardened to restrict SSH/RDP access to authorized sources only, and network isolation is configured for the ComputerEase VM prior to integration build. The client's IT team or GCP administrator performs the actual firewall and network changes.
Out of ScopeDataSkate will not administer or modify GCP firewall rules or networking configuration directly. DataSkate will not manage GCP IAM roles or project-level access controls. DataSkate will not provision or maintain the ComputerEase VM on GCP.
UC11

API Configuration via Deltek Support (event-triggered)

▼

Deltek Support Portal → ComputerEase · API Configuration · Event: integration project initiation / vendor ticket submission

1

⚠️ CRITICAL: Has a support ticket been submitted to Deltek to enable API access for ComputerEase and configure the CE Live Service relay? If so, what is the current ticket status and expected resolution date?

2

What version of the ComputerEase API is currently licensed or available in your environment — and is a sandbox or test instance of ComputerEase available for integration testing separate from production?

3

Does your Deltek support contract include API enablement as a standard feature, or is there an additional licensing or professional services cost associated with enabling the CE Live Service relay?

→ See Section 3.11 for the pre-filled UC11 field mapping table.

In ScopeDataSkate will provide technical specifications and API requirements documentation to support the client's Deltek support ticket submission, and will validate API connectivity and CE Live Service relay configuration once enabled.
Assumes Pre-existsThe client submits the Deltek support ticket and manages the vendor relationship. ComputerEase API access (v26+) and CE Live Service relay are enabled and confirmed operational before integration build begins. A sandbox environment with production parity is available for testing.
Out of ScopeDataSkate will not submit or manage the Deltek support ticket on the client's behalf. DataSkate will not negotiate Deltek licensing terms or API enablement costs. DataSkate will not configure the CE Live Service relay itself — this is a Deltek-administered action.
UC12

Deposit and Payment Terms Entry (event-triggered)

▼

HD Portal (Home Depot Service Center) → ComputerEase · Deposit · Event: signed contract with deposit confirmed in HD Portal

1

How does Ashley currently identify that a deposit has been received in HD Portal — is there a specific status field, report, or notification in the HD Portal backend that signals deposit confirmation?

2

What deposit and payment terms fields are entered into ComputerEase — for example, deposit amount, deposit date, payment schedule, total contract value, and payment method?

3

In ComputerEase, are deposit and payment terms stored at the job record level, or are they entered into a separate billing or accounts receivable module?

→ See Section 3.12 for the pre-filled UC12 field mapping table.

In ScopeDataSkate will build a flow that detects deposit confirmation status in HD Portal and automatically writes the deposit amount and payment terms to the corresponding ComputerEase job record via API, eliminating Ashley's manual entry step.
Assumes Pre-existsHD Portal API credentials are obtained from the HD Portal team (Marius) and the deposit status field is accessible via API. ComputerEase API access is enabled by Deltek support with CE Live Service relay configured. A matching ComputerEase job record exists at the time of deposit entry.
Out of ScopeDataSkate will not process or reconcile actual payment transactions. DataSkate will not integrate with any payment gateway or banking system. DataSkate will not manage accounts receivable workflows or invoice generation within ComputerEase.

Potential Flows — Not Priced in This Proposal

The flows below were identified during discovery as automation opportunities but are not included in the current proposal scope. Review each and indicate whether you would like to add it to scope for pricing.

IDFlow + RationalePriorityScope Decision
PF1 Automated Deposit Verification and Job Trigger
HD Portal → ComputerEase · Entity: Deposit

Ashley currently manually checks HD Portal backend reporting to find deposits and update Salesforce. An automated flow could verify deposit status via API and trigger job entry in ComputerEase without manual intervention, reducing data entry errors and accelerating job processing time. 		Evaluate
PF2 Quote Line Item Validation and Product Matching
Salesforce → ComputerEase · Entity: Quote Line Item

Quote line items in Salesforce contain product bundle data (material type, picket type, post caps, gates) that must be validated against contract specifications. An automated flow could extract quote line items, validate against master data in ComputerEase, and flag discrepancies before job entry — reducing rework caused by mismatched product configurations. 		Evaluate
PF3 Intelligent Document Processing for Contract Validation
HD Portal → Salesforce · Entity: Contract

Contract documents (299A, 299B, 118) are currently manually reviewed by Ashley for compliance. An IDP flow could automatically extract contract data, validate against business rules (permit date, deposit amount matching, signature legibility), and flag exceptions for manual review — reducing compliance risk and review time. 		Evaluate

Section 4 — Volume and Performance

This section captures transaction volume, performance requirements, and system resilience expectations across all integration flows.

4.1 — Transaction Volume

23

What is the expected transaction volume per flow? (e.g., leads per day, jobs per week, contracts per month)

→ Inferred from Home Depot service center operations (seasonal, lead-driven business model). Adjust based on actual historical volume from HD Portal and Salesforce.

4.2 — Peak Load and Seasonal Patterns

24

What are the peak load times and seasonal patterns? (e.g., time of day, day of week, seasonal spikes)

→ Typical for construction/home services industry. Confirm against actual HD Portal traffic logs and Salesforce activity reports.

4.3 — Latency Requirements

25

⚠️ CRITICAL: What is the maximum acceptable latency (delay) per flow type? (e.g., lead sync must complete within X minutes, contract generation within Y hours)

→ Scheduled polling flows (UC1) tolerate 10–15 min delay. Event-driven flows (UC2, UC4, UC9) require <60 sec. Manual flows (UC5, UC6, UC7, UC8, UC12) tolerate 24-hour SLA.

4.4 — Uptime and Availability SLA

26

What is the required uptime SLA (Service Level Agreement)? (e.g., 99.5%, 99.9%, 99.99%)

→ DataSkate standard for business-critical integrations. Escalate to 99.9% if revenue impact >$10K/hour downtime.

4.5 — Payload Size and Data Volume

27

What is the typical payload size range per transaction? (e.g., lead record ~2 KB, contract PDF ~5 MB)

→ JSON payloads are small (<5 KB). PDF contracts are largest (2–8 MB). Flag if DocHub or IDP has hard limits (e.g., 50-page, 10 MB max).

4.6 — Failure Recovery and Checkpointing

28

On sync failure, should the integration resume from the last successful checkpoint or restart from the beginning?

→ Checkpoint-based recovery is mandatory for UC1 (Lead Sync) to avoid duplicate lead ingestion. Event-driven flows (UC2, UC4, UC5) use idempotency keys.

4.7 — Worst-Case Batch Volume (Offline Recovery)

29

If the integration is offline for a weekend (48 hours), what is the worst-case record count that must be processed in the recovery batch?

→ Lead sync dominates volume due to 10-min polling frequency. Event-driven flows have lower backlog. Confirm HD Portal can buffer 48-hour lead queue without data loss.

4.8 — Performance Monitoring and Alerting

30

What performance metrics should trigger alerts? (e.g., latency >5 min, error rate >1%, backlog >1000 records)

→ Define thresholds per flow type. Recommend: latency alerts at 50% of max acceptable, error rate >0.5%, backlog >500 records.

4.9 — Concurrent User Load and API Rate Limits

31

How many concurrent users or API calls per second must the integration support?

→ Small team (sales reps + operations). Polling thread is single-threaded. Confirm Salesforce API rate limits (100 req/sec standard) and ComputerEase API throttling.

4.10 — Data Retention and Archive Policy

32

How long should integration logs, audit trails, and transaction records be retained? (e.g., 90 days, 1 year, 7 years)

→ Typical: 1 year operational logs, 7 years financial/contract records. Confirm with compliance and legal teams.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.bodyHtml:
Section 6 — Error Handling

This section defines how DataSkate will handle failures, retries, data loss prevention, and recovery across all integration flows. Error handling strategy must account for the mix of real-time syncs (lead polling), event-driven manual entry (job creation, contracts), and infrastructure dependencies (GCP, Deltek API).

6.1 — Retry Strategy & Dead Letter Queue

32

When a target system is unavailable or rejects a message, what is the desired behavior: retry with backoff, queue for later delivery, or fail immediately?

→ Applies to all 12 confirmed flows. Lead sync (UC1) will re-poll on next 10-min cycle regardless; event-driven flows (UC2–UC9, UC12) depend on DLQ for recovery.

6.2 — Message Expiry & Queue Retention

33

How long should messages remain in the retry queue before being discarded or escalated?

→ Job creation (UC2, UC3, UC12) and contracts (UC4, UC7) are financial-adjacent; longer retention reduces revenue leakage risk.

6.3 — Failure Notification & Escalation

34

⚠️ CRITICAL: Who should be notified when a flow fails, and via what channel (email, Slack, PagerDuty, etc.)? Include primary operational contact and DataSkate on-call.

→ No named contacts provided in discovery. Confirm Ashley's email, Slack workspace, and whether PagerDuty is available. DataSkate on-call: raghuram@dataskate.ai (architect).

6.4 — Data Loss Prevention Strategy

35

For each flow, is zero data loss required, or is best-effort acceptable? Differentiate by flow type.

→ Peerless Fence operates under Home Depot's compliance framework; contract and job records are audit-critical.

6.5 — Idempotency & Duplicate Prevention

36

Must all flows be idempotent (safe to replay without creating duplicates)? How will External IDs be used to prevent duplicate records?

→ Critical for manual entry flows (UC3, UC5, UC6, UC7, UC8, UC12) where Ashley may re-enter data during recovery.

6.6 — Rollback & Partial Failure Handling

37

For multi-step flows (e.g., job header + customer + worksheet in UC2), if one step fails, should the entire transaction roll back, or is partial retry acceptable?

→ UC2 (Job Entry with Budget Data) and UC3 (Customer Record Creation) are separate events; UC6 (Job Status Attachment) is manual and can be retried independently.

→ Recommend daily DLQ dashboard for Ashley; weekly escalation to Raghuram for unresolved 7-day messages.

  2. GCP Firewall Security Vulnerability (P0): Current rules allow SSH/RDP from anywhere. Must be hardened to restrict access to authorized IPs only and configure network isolation for ComputerEase VM before any production deployment. Blocks UC10 and all downstream ComputerEase flows.
  3. Salesforce API User Permissions (P0): Designated API user permissions not yet confirmed. Admin must verify full access to configure integrations and establish read-only API user for ComputerEase sync. Blocks UC1, UC2, UC4, UC5, UC8, UC9.
  4. Home Depot Portal API Credentials (P0): Credentials from Marius (HD Portal team) not yet obtained. Lead generation API must support 10-minute sync frequency. Webhook vs. polling mechanism for real-time updates unresolved. Blocks UC1, UC5, UC9, UC12, PF1, PF3.
  5. DocHub Digital Signature Configuration (P0): DocHub must be configured for contract types 299A, 299B, 118. Document storage/retrieval API for Salesforce integration not yet established. Blocks UC4, UC7, PF3.
  6. ComputerEase Modernization Assessment (P1): Legacy application; technical debt and modernization potential must be evaluated early. Impacts long-term maintainability of UC2, UC3, UC6, UC7, UC8, UC11, UC12.
  7. Salesforce Sandbox Limitations (P1): Sandbox environment parity with production not confirmed. Robust testing strategy required for production-only features. Affects UC1, UC2, UC4, UC5, UC8, UC9.
  8. Real-Time Lead Sync Feasibility (P1): 10-minute polling frequency from HD Portal to Salesforce (UC1) may not meet business expectations for lead freshness. Webhook alternative not yet scoped or costed. Impacts UC1 and PF1.
  9. IDP Integration for Contract Extraction (P1): Automated document extraction and validation for contract compliance (PF3) requires IDP scope definition. Currently out of scope but flagged for future consideration.
  10. Quote Line Item Business Rules (P1): Clear mapping logic for quote line items (product bundles: material type, picket type, post caps, gates) from HD Portal → Salesforce → ComputerEase not yet defined. Affects UC5, UC2, PF2.
  11. Process Automation Prioritization (P1): Manual tasks (UC3, UC5, UC6, UC7, UC8, UC12) must be prioritized by impact and frequency. Current scope is manual; automation roadmap needed post-launch.
  12. User Provisioning and Permission Models (P2): Access control across Salesforce, ComputerEase, HD Portal, DocHub, GCP must be verified and documented. Single admin SPOFs identified (Ashley for manual workflows).
  13. Multi-Environment Deployment Strategy (P2): Read-only access in sandboxes vs. controlled write access in production must be documented. GCP, Salesforce, ComputerEase, HD Portal all require environment-specific configuration.
